_about: Radiation planning layer along the route (team document 'Route Radiation Planning Layer', 15 Nov 2026). FORECAST only: it says when and where, never raises an alarm; the dosimeter (MEASURED) always wins; solar particle events are LIVE only (GOES). AE9/AP9, OLTARIS and SGP4 were not run: the forecast here is a SAMPLE model calibrated as noted per case. Colour classes use the radiation document's dose-rate caution limit; no new limit is made here.

classes._about: Forecast absorbed dose rate (mGy/day) compared with the radiation_rate caution limit (mSv/day, deep space) at quality factor Q = 1 (open item: the document does not say how to convert). The radiation document has no red dose-rate limit, so the forecast has no red class.

extraRatio.openItem: ε (extra = belt component above ε × GCR) is the team's choice; the document gives none. Placeholder 1.

gcrUGyH.basis: ISS DOSTEL-1 RadLab week (real, April 2022): minimum and 90th percentile of the 5-minute means = low- and high-latitude background

saa.basis: SAMPLE outline and peak (DOSTEL maximum 605 µGy/h); drift 0.3°/year west (SPENVIS)

uncertainty.basis: ISSCREM agreement with measurements: ±10 % GCR, ±20 % trapped

moon.label: Lunar transit (Artemis I type)
moon.beltBasis: approximate belt altitudes (SAMPLE); trajectory profile SAMPLE

innerPeakUGyMin.basis: Artemis I, inner belt: 69 µGy/min most shielded vs 240 and 287 µGy/min least shielded (George et al. 2024)

attitudeFactor.basis: changing the spacecraft attitude in the belts cut dose rates by about 50 % (NASA)

lunarShadow.basis: GCR about one third lower near the Moon (George et al. 2024); start distance SAMPLE

moon.outerBeltNote: Outer (electron) belt: no dose number in the source; shaded only

mars.label: Mars transit
mars.note: Almost only GCR; no position-bound hot spot to paint (document). Solar particle events cannot be mapped: live GOES strip only.
mars.sepBasis: NOAA SWPC: SEP event threshold ≥10 MeV at 10 pfu

evaRisk._about: EVA radiation risk index (ERI), team design 15 Nov 2026 (proposal, not a NASA standard). Built only from numbers the project already has: the radiation document's caution dose rate and its operational steps 0.5 / 0.8 / 1.0, the person's dose ledger, and the NOAA SEP threshold. ERI = max(R_route, R_dose, R_sep).

parts.route: R_route = highest upper-bound FORECAST dose rate during the planned EVA ÷ the radiation document's caution dose rate (1.3 mSv/day, deep space). 1.0 = the EVA reaches the dose rate the document already calls high.
parts.dose: R_dose = the person's worst ratio in the radiation ledger (career, 30-day organ, solar event) — someone close to a limit should not add EVA dose.
parts.sep: R_sep = 1.0 while a solar particle event runs (GOES ≥10 MeV at or above 10 pfu, NOAA SWPC); 0 otherwise.

evaRisk.limitNote: Limit = 0.8, the radiation document's Warning step: at or above it no EVA is planned in that window and the measures below are taken.

levels.advice: No radiation objection to EVA in this window.
EVA possible: tell the planner, keep the EVA short, stay near the airlock or shielding, watch the dosimeter.
Do not plan EVA in this window: move it to the next green window and prepare the shelter.
No EVA: crew outside return to the airlock now; everyone goes to the most shielded place (shelter).

evaRisk.authority: Decision support only. The final go / no-go is given by the flight director with the flight surgeon and the radiation officer (on a deep-space mission without real-time link: the commander with the crew medical officer).
